features.note: OPEN shot: two front vertical rails fully visible with a clearly regular punched U-slot hole pattern running the full height. Spacing reads as EIA 42U density. Rails are dark-metallic, positioned symmetrically at the front face. Right rail partially occluded by the cabinet right post but the slot rhythm is still legible. Rear rails not confirmed — interior depth obscured by side panels; deferred to voxel pass. Decisive improvement over attempt 2 (plain posts).

MESH shot: dense, regular hex/round perforation alpha pattern covers the entire door face. Reads unmistakably as perforated mesh, not a solid panel. Dark painted skin behind the open-area perf is visible. Hinge seam on the left edge is present.

GLASS shot: door is clearly translucent — interior left rail with slot pattern is readable through the glass. Blue LED edge-strip glows distinctly along the full door-frame perimeter (left, top, and bottom edges all lit). The emissive blue read is the single clearest Panduit-aisle identity cue in the set. Opacity is low enough that the rail reads through without the door becoming invisible.

MESH + GLASS shots: small rectangular black protrusion on the leading (right) edge at mid-height, clearly distinct from the door surface and not a painted decal. Reads as a graspable lever. Geometry is minimal — more of a tab than a shaped lever; adequate for blockout, should be refined in voxel pass.

important_features.note: All three shots: tall freestanding cabinet with correct ~3.3:1 H:W aspect for a 42U class unit. White plinth strip at base, top cap present. Small caster nubs visible at the four bottom corners. Cabinet is floor-standing, not floating. Silhouette reads convincingly as a datacenter aisle cabinet.

defects: Rear mounting rails not confirmed visible in any shot — open shot shows only the front-pair rails; interior depth behind the side panels is opaque. Voxel pass must expose or confirm the rear rail pair.
Lever handle is a minimal rectangular tab rather than a shaped lever form — proportionally small and low in lever-body detail.
Right front rail slot pattern partially occluded by the right cabinet post in the open shot — legible but not fully framed.
Glass shot interior content sparse — only the left front rail reads through the glass; rear rails and any cable-management structure are not visible.
corrections: Voxel pass: sculpt lever handle into a proper lever form (elongated grip bar + return, not a flat tab).
Voxel pass: confirm rear mounting rails exist and are visible through an open or partial-open view.
Voxel pass: consider thinning/shortening the right cabinet post or nudging camera azimuth to expose the right front rail fully.
Lighting pass: tune emissiveIntensity on the LED edge-strip so the glow halos outward from the frame perimeter (currently the strip itself is bright but lacks a soft spread).
